J1.evidence: Verse gloss: TR renders 'ما بالُها بالليلِ زالَ زوالَها' as 'Allah onun gidişini gidersin' (may Allah remove her departure), which contradicts the author's own explanation right after: 'كأنه قال: أزالَ اللَّهُ الليلَ زوالَها' (may Allah make the NIGHT pass away as she passes away; الليل is the object, زوالها a cognate accusative). TR thus glosses the verse against the text it is cited for (EN 'may [the night] pass away as she passes' follows the source). Also 'أزال الله الليل زوالها' itself is left untranslated in TR. Rest of TR (أوقد = yaktı, الذي = çoğul, هم صم بكم عمي ref' ibtida, حوله zarf) is faithful.

J2.evidence: Verse gloss of 'ما بالُها بالليلِ زالَ زوالَها' is rendered 'Allah onun gidişini gidersin' (God remove HER departure), but the source itself glosses it 'أزالَ اللَّهُ الليلَ زوالَها' (God made the NIGHT pass, as her passing): TR makes زوالها the thing removed and drops الليل as object. J2.evidence: In لان ايا ها هنا اسم the word ايا is not a typo: it is أيًّا, the accusative of أيّ as ism of لأنّ (cf. يا أيُّها الرجل just before). Quoting the particle in its citation form 'أيّ' is a correct rendering of the same word, not a silent correction of the source. Rest of TR (مَن lafẓ/maʿnā, ومن تقنت, ما جاءت حاجتك, رُبّ من / رُبّ ما, هذا ما لدي عتيد, نعمّا, the كمثل الذي استوقد note) is faithful.
